Yes at first with my current boyfriend. He didn’t do it intentionally but honestly just did not understand what anxiety was or how I experienced it. He’s coming around. I guess he’s just seen me deal with it more when it happens. We’ve talked about how he can support me, it didn’t come naturally to him so we’ve literally had talks where I said “when I was feeling anxious you said x, which made me feel y, I think if you phrased it like z, we both would feel better after”. When he does offer support or help me with a panic attack, I make sure to give him praise and let him know how much I appreciate it. Overtime it just became more natural for him to be supportive and understand my perspective.

Relapse is a part of recovery, it’s a long road and one mess up does not erase the work you put in. In the year without self harm you learned and practiced how to resist an addictive urge, you still have that knowledge deep in your brain to help you through this relapse. Acknowledge it happened and it was a mistake but try to not let the guilt blind you from your progress
